a1-to-be-nationalities-01.note: Now that you can state where people are from, learn how to describe who they are and what they do.

challenge.q: Sofía ___ from Colombia and she ___ a brilliant graphic designer.
challenge.hint: Sofía is singular (she), so use 'is' in both slots.

a1-to-be-identities-01.note: Careful Spanish transfer trap: In English we use 'to be' for age and emotions, but 'have got' for possessions.

challenge.q: Sofía ___ twenty-five years old, and she ___ two cats.
challenge.hint: Age takes 'to be' ('is 25'), while pets take 'has got'!

a1-have-got-01.note: From what you have to who belongs to who: master the English apostrophe -'s.

challenge.q: This is ___ iguana. She has got twenty mangos.
challenge.hint: Add 's to the owner: Abuela Carmen's iguana.

a1-family-possessive-s-01.note: Learn to replace names with my, your, his, her, their without hesitation.

challenge.q: Ben loves Cartagena. ___ favorite place is the old clock tower.
challenge.hint: Ben is a man, so his possessive adjective is 'His'.

a1-pronouns-possessives-01.nextTitle: Object Pronouns (me, him, her, us, them)
a1-pronouns-possessives-01.note: When the person receives the action instead of doing it: I -> me, he -> him, they -> them.

challenge.q: Kenji loves arepas. Abuela Carmen makes ___ for ___ every morning.
challenge.hint: Arepas are the object ('them'), and Kenji receives them ('him').

a1-articles-01.note: Articles 'a/an' only work with singular nouns. Now discover what happens when nouns become plural.

challenge.q: Ben saw one ___ and three ___ in the city park.
challenge.hint: 'Child' is an irregular plural: one child, three children!

a1-plural-nouns-01.note: Point at things near and far in singular and plural: This, That, These, Those.

challenge.q: ___ mangos here in my basket are fresh, but ___ over there look old.
challenge.hint: 'These' for nearby plural, 'those' for distant plural.

a1-demonstratives-01.note: English adjectives never change for gender or plural, and always go BEFORE the noun!

challenge.q: Sofía lives in a ___ and designs ___ posters.
challenge.hint: Adjective goes before the noun and never takes an -s: 'beautiful house', 'colorful posters'.

a1-present-simple-routines-01.note: Take your daily routines to the next level: specify how often with always, usually, sometimes, and never.

challenge.q: Abuela Carmen ___ at five in the morning.
challenge.hint: Adverbs of frequency go BEFORE the main verb: 'always wakes up'.

a1-present-simple-frequency-01.nextTitle: Present Simple — Likes, Hobbies & Free Time
a1-present-simple-frequency-01.note: Learn how to talk about what you enjoy: verbs of liking + -ing (like, love, enjoy, hate).

challenge.q: Kenji ___ photos of the colonial balconies.
challenge.hint: Third person takes -s ('loves') and 'love' is followed by the gerund ('taking').

a1-present-simple-likes-01.note: Master the secret weapon of English: the auxiliaries DO and DOES for negatives and questions.

challenge.q: ___ Ben ___ coffee in the morning? No, he drinks tea.
challenge.hint: 'Does' already marks third person, so the main verb stays base: 'Does he drink?'

a1-present-simple-neg-questions-01.note: The ultimate A1 contrast: What you do habitually (routines) vs what you are doing right now.

challenge.q: Kenji usually ___ breakfast at eight, but today he ___ at nine.
challenge.hint: 'Usually' calls for Present Simple, while 'today / right now' calls for Present Continuous!

a1-present-continuous-01.note: Bridge from present continuous to the future: use 'be going to' to announce your next goals.

challenge.q: Sofía bought her plane tickets. She ___ visit London in June.
challenge.hint: A pre-arranged intention with tickets already bought uses 'is going to'!

a2-verb-to-be-past-01.note: You can say where you were (was/were). Now learn how to describe any action in the past.

challenge.q: Yesterday, Ben ___ around the walled city and ___ at a cafe.
challenge.hint: Add -ed for regular past: 'walked', and double consonant for 'stopped'.

a2-past-simple-regular-01.note: Not all verbs take -ed! Meet the 126 verbs that change their vowel or form in the past.

challenge.q: Kenji ___ an email to his mother and ___ a souvenir.
challenge.hint: 'Write' becomes 'wrote' and 'buy' becomes 'bought'.

a2-past-simple-irregular-01.nextTitle: Past Continuous vs Past Simple (when / while)
a2-past-simple-irregular-01.note: Combine an action in progress in the past with a sudden interrupting event.

challenge.q: While Ben ___ his tea, the doorbell ___.
challenge.hint: The background ongoing action takes was/were + -ing; the interruption takes Past Simple!

a2-past-continuous-vs-simple-01.nextTitle: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Which One?
a2-past-continuous-vs-simple-01.note: The #1 grammar dilemma in English: finished past time vs open, living experience.

challenge.q: I ___ to Cartagena in 2022, but Kenji ___ there three times.
challenge.hint: 'In 2022' is a closed past time (went), but total life experiences take Present Perfect (has been)!

b1-present-perfect-vs-past-simple-01.nextTitle: Present Perfect Continuous — for / since / just
b1-present-perfect-vs-past-simple-01.note: Emphasize how long an action has been happening non-stop: 'I have been studying for 2 hours'.

challenge.q: Sofía is exhausted because she ___ posters all afternoon.
challenge.hint: Focus on the duration and immediate physical effect: Present Perfect Continuous!

b1-present-perfect-continuous-01.note: Travel further back in time: describe an action that happened BEFORE another past action.

challenge.q: When Ben arrived at the station, the train ___ already ___.
challenge.hint: The train left before Ben arrived: Past Perfect (had + participle)!

b1-will-vs-going-to-01.note: Take future predictions into hypothetical worlds: If it rains, I will stay. If I were you, I would go.

challenge.q: If I ___ more free time, I ___ travel across South America.
challenge.hint: Second conditional for an imaginary present situation: If + past simple, would + verb.

b1-conditionals-0-1-2-01.note: Step into the past impossible: talk about what could have happened, but didn't.

challenge.q: If Ben ___ his alarm, he ___ the flight.
challenge.hint: Third conditional: If + had + participle, would have + participle.

b1-passive-voice-01.note: From 'The car was washed' (passive) to 'I had my car washed' (you arranged for someone else to do it).

challenge.q: Sofía didn't paint her office herself. She ___ it ___ by professionals.
challenge.hint: Causative structure: have + object + past participle.

b2-third-conditional-01.nextTitle: Mixed Conditionals — Past Causes, Present Results
b2-third-conditional-01.note: Blend the rules: a past decision that creates an ongoing reality right now.

challenge.q: If I ___ German at school, I ___ able to read this contract now.
challenge.hint: Past action (had studied) with a present result right now (would be)!

b2-relative-clauses-01.note: Transform relative clauses into high-scoring C1 prose: 'The man who was sitting' -> 'Sitting by the window'.

challenge.q: ___ by the breathtaking sunset, Ben took dozens of photos.
challenge.hint: Passive past participle clause describing how Ben felt.

b2-reported-speech-01.note: Add dramatic weight to your statements: 'I do want to help you' and 'So compelling was her argument'.

challenge.q: Believe me, I ___ apologize to Kenji yesterday!
challenge.hint: Use emphatic 'did' + base verb in affirmative past statements.

c1-emphatic-structures-01.note: The crown jewel of Cambridge C1 exam transformations: Rarely have I seen, Never before did he speak.

challenge.q: Rarely ___ such dedication in a language learner.
challenge.hint: After negative adverbs like 'Rarely', invert the auxiliary and subject: 'have I witnessed'.

c1-inversion-01.note: Re-frame any sentence to spotlight the exact piece of information you want to emphasize.

challenge.q: ___ surprised everyone was Ben's flawless Spanish.
challenge.hint: What-cleft: 'What surprised everyone was...' focuses on the noun clause.
